title: NY State Assembly · District 30
area: Western Queens, including Woodside, Maspeth, Elmhurst and Jackson Heights.

context.text: Incumbent Steven Raga did not seek re-election to this seat, running instead for NY State Senate District 12. Patrick Martinez won a three-way Democratic primary on June 23, 2026 by seven votes over Shamsul Haque (2,784 to 2,777, with Somnath Ghimire receiving 718) after an automatic recount triggered by an initial 13-vote margin. Brandon Castro, who ran against Raga for this seat in 2024, advanced unopposed on the Republican and Conservative Party lines.

candidates.name: Patrick Martinez
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary by seven votes after an automatic recount.

summary.text: Patrick Martinez is the Democratic nominee for the open NY State Assembly District 30 seat. A Democratic District Leader for the 30th Assembly District and member of Queens Community Board 2, he grew up in Elmhurst and worked in the tech startup field before entering local party and community roles. He won a close three-way Democratic primary with backing from the Queens County Democratic Party and local unions.

background.text: Describes himself as born and raised in Elmhurst, Queens, where he attended local public schools before Stuyvesant High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Middlebury College in 2009, majoring in Latin American Studies, and a graduate degree from Baruch College in 2020.
According to his Ballotpedia survey response, he studied in Buenos Aires, taught English in Costa Rica, and after graduating taught elementary school in Incheon, Korea.

Back in New York, he worked in the tech startup world, including with Coalition for Queens on tech training and job placement for underrepresented groups; Ballotpedia lists his profession as marketing director.
Moved back to Woodside and joined Queens Community Board 2 in 2022, where he focuses on land use and the OneLIC task force.
Serves as Democratic District Leader for Assembly District 30 and says he helped build the Queens Forward Democratic Club.

Is the nephew of former U.S. Rep. Joe Crowley, according to the Queens Daily Eagle and the Queens Chronicle; the Queens County Democratic Party endorsed him before he launched his campaign, according to City & State as reported by the Chronicle.
Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary by seven votes over Shamsul Haque after an automatic recount; the Queens Daily Eagle reported union support for his campaign.

priorities.text: Tenant protections and housing affordability, including protecting Mitchell-Lama affordability, expanding property tax relief, and requiring deeply affordable units in new development.

Public investment in schools, transit and infrastructure, including full funding for public schools, expanded after-school programs, accelerated subway and bus improvements, and climate resiliency against flooding.
Workers' rights, including strengthening labor protections and supporting union growth.

positions.summary: Says he supports comprehensive housing reform that includes stronger tenant protections and good-cause eviction.
Says he supports upzoning near transit with affordability mandates as part of housing reform.
positions.quote: upzoning near transit with affordability mandates

positions.summary: Answered "Yes. I support full access to reproductive healthcare, including abortion, without restriction" when asked on the Jim Owles Liberal Democratic Club questionnaire (March 2026) whether he supports the unrestricted right to reproductive care and abortion.
positions.quote: I support full access to reproductive healthcare, including abortion, without restriction.

positions.summary: Says he will work to pass the New York for All Act, which would limit cooperation by local agencies with federal immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: In office, I will fight to pass New York For All to prevent local agencies from cooperating with ICE.

positions.summary: Answered yes on the Jim Owles Liberal Democratic Club questionnaire to supporting legislation that raises taxes on the richest New Yorkers and large corporations.
positions.quote: We must ensure the wealthiest pay their fair share to fund housing, education, healthcare, and social services.

positions.summary: Says he would work to pass the New York Health Act.
positions.quote: everyone should have access to healthcare regardless of documentation status, and passing the New York Health Act will ensure just that.

positions.summary: Lists passing Universal Childcare, alongside strengthening 3K and Pre-K, among his education priorities.
positions.quote: This, coupled with passing Universal Childcare and strengthening our 3K and Pre-K programs, will help not only our children, but our entire community to thrive.

statements.quote: Climate Change is the single biggest long-term threat to our society and economy.
statements.context: On his campaign website's Priorities page

candidates.researchNotes: Positions drawn from his Jim Owles Liberal Democratic Club questionnaire (March 2026) and his campaign website's Priorities page. He gave no statement on several guide issues (e.g., guns, police funding, school choice).

candidates.name: Brandon Castro

summary.text: Brandon Castro is the Republican, Conservative, Arts & Culture and Reform Party nominee for the open NY State Assembly District 30 seat. A Queens College graduate and former NYC Small Business Services liaison, he lost to Steven Raga in the 2024 general election for this seat. He is running on education and workforce reform, infrastructure investment and public safety.

background.text: Born in New York City; describes himself as a lifelong Queens resident and the son of Ecuadorian immigrants, educated in New York City public schools.
Graduated from Queens Technical High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the City University of New York, Queens College, in 2023.
Worked as a liaison for the NYC Department of Small Business Services, supporting and assisting small businesses, and says he has also worked on grassroots campaigns.
Ran against incumbent Steven Raga for this seat in the November 2024 general election, running on the Republican and Common Sense Party lines; Raga won 60.4% to Castro's 39.3%.
Won the 2026 Republican nomination for the seat, which the Queens Daily Eagle and Queens Chronicle describe as setting up a November race against Patrick Martinez.

priorities.text: Education and workforce reform, including investing in trade schools and vocational training, keeping the SHSAT, and expanding merit-based financial aid.
Infrastructure investment, including upgrading sewer and stormwater systems and improving public transit, saying growth requires that "infrastructure and public safety must come first."
priorities.quote: I believe in smart growth, but infrastructure and public safety must come first.

priorities.text: Public safety, including increasing NYPD staffing and training to restore a visible police presence.

positions.summary: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, says safety requires increasing NYPD manpower and investing in better training; Branch's summary of his platform also describes support for additional NYPD funding.
positions.quote: That means increasing NYPD manpower, investing in better training, and ensuring officers can protect our communities effectively and responsibly.

statements.quote: While the state pushes new housing, too many of our communities are being left behind with crumbling infrastructure.
statements.context: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.researchNotes: Castro has no campaign website that could be loaded; positions come from his 2026 Ballotpedia survey and a Branch summary. His 2026 answers do not address most guide issues.
